correctness.rationale: For \(1<p\le2\), Clarkson\'s conjugate-exponent inequality gives \(A^q+B^q\le2(\kappa^p+\tau^p)^{q/p}\) for \(A=\|\kappa x+\tau y\|_p\), \(B=\|\kappa x-\tau y\|_p\), and \(q=p/(p-1)\). AM--GM then gives \(\sqrt{AB}\le(\kappa^p+\tau^p)^{1/p}\). Disjoint coordinate unit vectors attain equality. The endpoints \(p=1\) and \(p=\infty\) follow from the triangle inequality and explicit two-coordinate witnesses. At \(p=2\) the branch equals the published super-Hilbert formula. All quantifiers and endpoint cases are included, and no finite experiment is used as proof.

originality.rationale: The focal source explicitly computes the same constant on classical sequence spaces only for the super-Hilbert range and supplies only universal bounds outside it. Exact-notation, formula, alias, and implication searches found no published record covering the full sub-Hilbert two-parameter product formula. The closest records concern different functionals (minimum, arithmetic mean, or four-term quadratic averages) and do not imply the required product upper bound. The 2008 ancestor is retained as a residual terminology risk rather than treated as evidence of absence.

Very recent or poorly indexed work may not yet appear in the checked databases.

value.rationale: The focal paper introduces a natural two-parameter geometric invariant and explicitly leaves its classical \(\ell_p\) calculation at \(p>2\). The new theorem fills the entire complementary range \(1\le p\le2\) plus the \(p=\infty\) endpoint, converting a partial example into a complete exact classical phase diagram. It also identifies the natural extremal transition at the Hilbert exponent: disjoint supports are sharp below \(2\), while the published branch above \(2\) uses a balanced two-coordinate configuration. This is a complete classification of a motivated family, not an arbitrary slice or a numerical recomputation.
